cases.name: build-lock runs the command given as words after `--`, keeps its exit and leaves no lock behind
cases.cmd: R={{FIX}}/bl-run-{{SID}}; rm -rf $R; mkdir -p $R && cd $R && git init -q && bash {{KIT}}/scripts/build-lock.sh -- sh -c 'echo built; exit 3'; echo "exit=$?|$(test -e .git/cctoolkit-build.lock && echo held || echo free)"

cases.name: build-lock passes each word intact, quotes and spaces included, and an `env` prefix carries a variable
cases.cmd:
R={{FIX}}/bl-argv-{{SID}}; rm -rf $R; mkdir -p $R && cd $R && git init -q && bash {{KIT}}/scripts/build-lock.sh -- env FOO='a b' sh -c 'printf "%s|%s
" "$FOO" "$1"' x '*.Catalog "Products".*'

cases.name: build-lock in a worktree takes the lock of the git common dir: a lock held there makes it wait, then exit 75 without running the command
cases.cmd: R={{FIX}}/bl-wt-{{SID}}; rm -rf $R $R-wt; mkdir -p $R && cd $R && git init -q && git config user.name eval && git config user.email eval@example.invalid && git config commit.gpgsign false && git commit -q --allow-empty -m init && git worktree add -q $R-wt && mkdir .git/cctoolkit-build.lock && date +%s > .git/cctoolkit-build.lock/since && cd $R-wt && bash {{KIT}}/scripts/build-lock.sh --wait 1 -- echo ran; e=$?; cd $R && git worktree remove --force $R-wt; echo "exit=$e"

cases.name: build-lock takes over a lock older than --stale
cases.cmd: R={{FIX}}/bl-stale-{{SID}}; rm -rf $R; mkdir -p $R && cd $R && git init -q && mkdir .git/cctoolkit-build.lock && echo 1 > .git/cctoolkit-build.lock/since && bash {{KIT}}/scripts/build-lock.sh --stale 60 -- echo ran

cases.name: build-lock with a --wait that is not seconds is a usage error
build-lock refuses a command passed as one quoted string without `--`: it would run through `eval`, out of the guards' sight
